label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Inverse Trigonometric Functions & Graph Symmetries
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — Inverse Trigonometric الدوال & التمثيل البياني Symmetries

body.en:
Principal Domains & Ranges: Because trigonometric functions are periodic and non-injective, their domains must be restricted to define inverse functions:

  • \(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\): Domain \([-1, 1]\), Range \([-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}]\). Odd function: \(\arcsin(-x) = -\arcsin(x)\).
  • \(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\): Domain \([-1, 1]\), Range \([0, \pi]\). Symmetry: \(\arccos(-x) = \pi - \arccos(x)\).
  • \(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\): Domain \(\mathbb{R}\), Range \((-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2})\). Odd function with horizontal asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\).

Cofunction Complementarity Identity: \[ \arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2} \quad \text{for all } x \in [-1, 1]. \] Derivatives via Implicit Differentiation: Let \(y = \arcsin x \implies \sin y = x\). Differentiating implicitly with respect to \(x\): \[ \cos y \frac{dy}{dx} = 1 \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{\cos y} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \sin^2 y}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}. \] Similarly: \[ \frac{d}{dx}(\arccos x) = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}, \qquad \frac{d}{dx}(\arctan x) = \frac{1}{1 + x^2}. \]

label.en: ▲ Level 2 Analytical Tools — Series Convergence & Variable Acceleration Kinematics
label.ar: ▲ Level 2 Analytical Tools — المتسلسلة Convergence & المتغير Acceleration Kinematics

body.en:
D'Alembert's Ratio Test: Let \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n\) be a series with non-zero terms. Evaluate the limiting ratio: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right|. \] Convergence Verdict:

  • If \(L < 1\): the series converges absolutely.
  • If \(L > 1\) (or \(L = \infty\)): the series diverges.
  • If \(L = 1\): the test is inconclusive (the series may converge or diverge; comparison or integral tests required).

Radius and Interval of Convergence: For a power series \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n (x - a)^n\), applying the ratio test yields \(|x - a| < R\), where \(R = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left|\frac{c_n}{c_{n+1}}\right|\) is the radius of convergence. Endpoints \(x = a \pm R\) must be tested individually.

Variable Acceleration Kinematics in AA HL: When acceleration is not constant, standard SUVAT equations fail. Acceleration can be expressed in terms of time \(t\), displacement \(s\), or velocity \(v\): \[ a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2s}{dt^2} = v\frac{dv}{ds} \quad \left( \text{via chain rule: } \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{ds}\frac{ds}{dt} = v\frac{dv}{ds} \right). \] Differential equations in kinematics:

  • If \(a = f(t)\): \(v(t) = \int f(t)\,dt\) and \(s(t) = \int v(t)\,dt\).
  • If \(a = f(v)\): To relate \(v\) and \(t\), separate \(\frac{dv}{dt} = f(v) \implies \int \frac{dv}{f(v)} = \int dt\). To relate \(v\) and \(s\), separate \(v\frac{dv}{ds} = f(v) \implies \int \frac{v\,dv}{f(v)} = \int ds\).
  • If \(a = f(s)\): Use \(v\frac{dv}{ds} = f(s) \implies \int v\,dv = \int f(s)\,ds \implies \frac{1}{2}v^2 = \int f(s)\,ds + C\).

label.en: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — Theorem: Real Quadratic Factorization & Paper 3 Mastery
label.ar: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — مبرهنة: Real Quadratic Factorization & Paper 3 Mastery

body.en:
Real Quadratic Factorization Theorem: Every polynomial \(P(z) \in \mathbb{R}[z]\) can be factored over \(\mathbb{R}\) into a product of linear real factors and irreducible real quadratic factors of the form \(z^2 - 2\text{Re}(z_k)z + |z_k|^2\).
For the cyclotomic polynomial \(z^{2m} - 1\): \[ z^{2m} - 1 = (z - 1)(z + 1) \prod_{k=1}^{m-1} \left( z^2 - 2z\cos\left(\frac{k\pi}{m}\right) + 1 \right). \] Proof Outline: Roots of \(z^{2m} = 1\) are \(e^{i k\pi / m}\) for \(k = -(m-1), \dots, m\). Pairing each root \(e^{i k\pi/m}\) with its complex conjugate \(e^{-i k\pi/m}\) gives: \[ (z - e^{i k\pi/m})(z - e^{-i k\pi/m}) = z^2 - 2z\cos\left(\frac{k\pi}{m}\right) + 1. \quad \blacksquare \]

Paper 3 Investigation Strategy & Heuristics: Paper 3 consists of two 55-mark extended, unstructured inquiries. Success requires a university-level investigative workflow:

  1. Identify the Invariant: Compute early terms (e.g. \(n = 1, 2, 3\)) explicitly. Look for geometric self-similarity, combinatorial symmetry, or telescoping sums.
  2. Lemma Construction: State your intermediate conjectures clearly before proving them. When an exam asks to 'show that', write out every intermediate algebraic factor.
  3. Asymptotic & Limiting Analysis: Relate discrete sequences to continuous integrals or Taylor expansions as \(n \to \infty\) (e.g. Riemann sum approximations \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\sum f(k/n) = \int_0^1 f(x)\,dx\)).

label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (AA HL — Additional Topics)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example AA.1 — Ratio Test & Interval of Convergence
label.ar: مثال محلول AA.1 — Ratio Test & Interval of Convergence

problem.en: Find the radius and exact interval of convergence of the power series \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(2x - 1)^n}{n \cdot 4^n}\).
problem.ar: أوجد نصف القطر and exact interval of convergence of the power المتسلسلة \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(2x - 1)^n}{n \cdot 4^n}\).

solution.en:
1. Apply D'Alembert's Ratio Test with \(a_n = \frac{(2x - 1)^n}{n \cdot 4^n}\): \[ \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right| = \left| \frac{(2x - 1)^{n+1}}{(n+1)4^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 4^n}{(2x - 1)^n} \right| = \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} \cdot \frac{n}{n+1}. \] 2. Take the limit as \(n \to \infty\): \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} \cdot \frac{n}{n+1} \right) = \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} \cdot 1 = \frac{|2x - 1|}{4}. \] 3. Require \(L < 1\) for absolute convergence: \[ \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} < 1 \implies |2x - 1| < 4 \implies -4 < 2x - 1 < 4 \implies -3 < 2x < 5 \implies -\frac{3}{2} < x < \frac{5}{2}. \] The radius of convergence is \(R = \frac{5/2 - (-3/2)}{2} = 2\).

4. Test Endpoints:
At \(x = \frac{5}{2}\): \(2x - 1 = 4\), so the series becomes \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{4^n}{n \cdot 4^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n}\) (the harmonic series, which diverges).
At \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\): \(2x - 1 = -4\), so the series becomes \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-4)^n}{n \cdot 4^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{n}\) (the alternating harmonic series, which converges by the Alternating Series Test).

Interval of Convergence: \(\left[ -\frac{3}{2}, \frac{5}{2} \right)\).
solution.ar:
1. Apply D'Alembert's Ratio Test with \(a_n = \frac{(2x - 1)^n}{n \cdot 4^n}\): \[ \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right| = \left| \frac{(2x - 1)^{n+1}}{(n+1)4^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 4^n}{(2x - 1)^n} \right| = \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} \cdot \frac{n}{n+1}. \] 2. Take the النهاية as \(n \to \infty\): \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} \cdot \frac{n}{n+1} \right) = \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} \cdot 1 = \frac{|2x - 1|}{4}. \] 3. Require \(L < 1\) for absolute convergence: \[ \frac{|2x - 1|}{4} < 1 \implies |2x - 1| < 4 \implies -4 < 2x - 1 < 4 \implies -3 < 2x < 5 \implies -\frac{3}{2} < x < \frac{5}{2}. \] The نصف القطر of convergence is \(R = \frac{5/2 - (-3/2)}{2} = 2\).

4. Test Endpoints:
At \(x = \frac{5}{2}\): \(2x - 1 = 4\), so the المتسلسلة becomes \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{4^n}{n \cdot 4^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n}\) (the harmonic المتسلسلة, which diverges).
At \(x = -\frac{3}{2}\): \(2x - 1 = -4\), so the المتسلسلة becomes \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-4)^n}{n \cdot 4^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{n}\) (the alternating harmonic المتسلسلة, which converges by the Alternating المتسلسلة Test).

Interval of Convergence: \(\left[ -\frac{3}{2}, \frac{5}{2} \right)\).

label.en: Worked Example AA.2 — Variable Acceleration Kinematics
label.ar: مثال محلول AA.2 — المتغير Acceleration Kinematics

problem.en: A particle moves in a straight line with acceleration \(a = -0.2 v^2\) m/s², where \(v > 0\) is its velocity in m/s. Given that its initial velocity at \(t = 0\) and \(s = 0\) is \(v_0 = 10\) m/s, find: (a) the velocity as a function of time \(t\); (b) the velocity as a function of displacement \(s\).
problem.ar: A particle moves in a straight line with acceleration \(a = -0.2 v^2\) m/s², حيث \(v > 0\) is its velocity in m/s. بما أن its initial velocity at \(t = 0\) and \(s = 0\) is \(v_0 = 10\) m/s, find: (a) the velocity as a الدالة of time \(t\); (b) the velocity as a الدالة of displacement \(s\).

solution.en:
(a) Velocity as a function of time \(t\):
Use \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = -0.2 v^2\). Separate variables: \[ \int \frac{dv}{v^2} = -0.2 \int dt \implies -\frac{1}{v} = -0.2 t + C_1 \implies \frac{1}{v} = 0.2 t - C_1. \] Apply initial condition \(v(0) = 10\): \[ \frac{1}{10} = -C_1 \implies C_1 = -0.1. \] Thus: \[ \frac{1}{v} = 0.2 t + 0.1 \implies v(t) = \frac{1}{0.2 t + 0.1} = \frac{10}{2t + 1} \text{ m/s}. \]

(b) Velocity as a function of displacement \(s\):
Use \(a = v\frac{dv}{ds} = -0.2 v^2\). Divide by \(v\) (since \(v > 0\)): \[ \frac{dv}{ds} = -0.2 v \implies \int \frac{dv}{v} = -0.2 \int ds \implies \ln v = -0.2 s + C_2. \] Apply initial condition \(s = 0, v = 10\): \[ \ln 10 = C_2. \] Therefore: \[ \ln v = -0.2 s + \ln 10 \implies \ln\left(\frac{v}{10}\right) = -0.2 s \implies v(s) = 10 e^{-0.2 s} \text{ m/s}. \]
solution.ar:
(a) Velocity as a الدالة of time \(t\):
Use \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = -0.2 v^2\). Separate المتغيرات: \[ \int \frac{dv}{v^2} = -0.2 \int dt \implies -\frac{1}{v} = -0.2 t + C_1 \implies \frac{1}{v} = 0.2 t - C_1. \] Apply initial condition \(v(0) = 10\): \[ \frac{1}{10} = -C_1 \implies C_1 = -0.1. \] وعليه: \[ \frac{1}{v} = 0.2 t + 0.1 \implies v(t) = \frac{1}{0.2 t + 0.1} = \frac{10}{2t + 1} \text{ m/s}. \]

(b) Velocity as a الدالة of displacement \(s\):
Use \(a = v\frac{dv}{ds} = -0.2 v^2\). Divide by \(v\) (since \(v > 0\)): \[ \frac{dv}{ds} = -0.2 v \implies \int \frac{dv}{v} = -0.2 \int ds \implies \ln v = -0.2 s + C_2. \] Apply initial condition \(s = 0, v = 10\): \[ \ln 10 = C_2. \] وبالتالي: \[ \ln v = -0.2 s + \ln 10 \implies \ln\left(\frac{v}{10}\right) = -0.2 s \implies v(s) = 10 e^{-0.2 s} \text{ m/s}. \]

question.en: Use the substitution \(x = 2\sin\theta\) to evaluate the exact definite integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx\).
question.ar: Use the substitution \(x = 2\sin\theta\) to احسب قيمة the exact definite integral \(\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx\).

solution.en:
1. Substitute \(x = 2\sin\theta \implies dx = 2\cos\theta\,d\theta\).
When \(x = 0\), \(\theta = 0\). When \(x = 1\), \(2\sin\theta = 1 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
2. Rewrite integrand: \[ \sqrt{4 - x^2} = \sqrt{4 - 4\sin^2\theta} = 2\sqrt{\cos^2\theta} = 2\cos\theta \quad (\text{since } \cos\theta > 0 \text{ on } [0, \pi/6]). \] 3. Substitute into the integral: \[ \int_0^1 \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx = \int_0^{\pi/6} (2\cos\theta)(2\cos\theta\,d\theta) = 4 \int_0^{\pi/6} \cos^2\theta\,d\theta. \] 4. Use double-angle identity \(\cos^2\theta = \frac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}\): \[ = 4 \int_0^{\pi/6} \frac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}\,d\theta = 2 \left[ \theta + \frac{\sin 2\theta}{2} \right]_0^{\pi/6} = 2\left( \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\sin(\pi/3)}{2} \right) = 2\left( \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \right) = \frac{\pi}{3} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}. \]

solution.ar: For the function \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - k}\) to have a removable discontinuity at \(x = 3\), the numerator and the denominator must both be zero at \(x = 3\). This means that \((x-3)\) must be a حلّل of both the numerator and the denominator. The numerator is \(x^2 - 9\), which حلّلs as \((x-3)(x+3)\). For the denominator to have a حلّل of \((x-3)\), we must have \(x - k = 0\) عندما \(x = 3\). وعليه، \(3 - k = 0\), which implies \(k = 3\). عندما \(k=3\), \(f(x) = \frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}\). For \(x eq 3\), \(f(x) = x+3\). The discontinuity at \(x=3\) is removable because the limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x \to 3\) exists (it is \(3+3=6\)), but \(f(3)\) is undefined. Common mistake: إذا كان one incorrectly assumes that the discontinuity is vertical, they might try to أوجد a vertical asymptote. However, a removable discontinuity occurs عندما a حلّل cancels out from the numerator and denominator.

Because the six trigonometric functions are periodic, they are not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\).
